claims.claim: Tail-color reduction: if D has no antiparallel pair, form an undirected graph whose edge {v,w} has color v whenever v→w. Every rainbow cycle in this graph is a directed cycle of D of the same length.
claims.evidence: On a rainbow cycle of length l, all l edge colors are endpoints of the cycle and are distinct, so every cycle vertex occurs exactly once as a tail. Thus every vertex has exactly one outgoing cycle edge, forcing a consistently oriented directed cycle of the same length.
Selecting one outgoing arc at every vertex and iterating produces a repeated vertex among n+1 terms. Taking the first repetition yields a simple directed cycle of length at most n=ceil(n/1).

An antiparallel pair gives a 2-cycle, within ceil(n/2) since n>=3. Otherwise, retaining two outgoing arcs per vertex gives n tail-color classes of size two. Theorem 1 stated in the authorized source, with p=0, gives a rainbow cycle of length at most ceil(n/2), and claim 0 transfers it to D.
claims.search_method: Authorized theorem-statement matching plus independent reduction audit

claims.evidence: Without antiparallel arcs, |A|<=n(n-1)/2, whereas minimum outdegree d>=n/2 gives |A|>=nd>=n²/2, a contradiction. Hence a 2-cycle exists; since d<=n-1 and d>=n/2, ceil(n/d)=2.

claims.claim: Every such D has a directed cycle of length at most n-d+1.
claims.evidence: For a longest simple directed path v1→...→vm, every outneighbor of vm lies on the path. The largest index j among at least d such outneighbors satisfies j>=d, and vm→vj together with the path from vj to vm is a cycle of length m-j+1<=n-d+1.

claims.claim: There is a universal C<=10^11 such that every D has directed girth at most Cn/d.
claims.evidence: The authorized source states the corresponding rainbow theorem with a universal C0<=10^11. In the oriented case, retain d outgoing arcs per vertex and apply claim 0. If an antiparallel pair exists, use its 2-cycle and replace C0 by max(C0,2), which remains at most 10^11 and satisfies 2<=Cn/d because d<n.
claims.search_method: Authorized theorem-statement matching plus independent reduction and exceptional-case audit

claims.claim: For each fixed d there is a constant alpha_d>0 such that every D has directed girth at most n/d+alpha_d.
claims.evidence: The authorized source states the additive rainbow-girth theorem for each fixed class size d. Claim 0 transfers it when D is oriented. An antiparallel pair is covered after enlarging the source constant to at least 1, since d<n implies 2<n/d+1.
claims.search_method: Authorized theorem-statement matching plus independent reduction and exceptional-case audit

claims.claim: If a counterexample exists, one of minimum order can be taken oriented, strongly connected, and exactly d-outregular; moreover d>=3 and K=ceil(n/d)>=3.
claims.evidence: Choose a globally minimum-order counterexample and delete excess outgoing arcs to make it d-outregular. It is oriented because K>=2. A sink strongly connected component retains all d outgoing arcs; if proper, its order n'<n and ceil(n'/d)<=K, so it would be a smaller counterexample. Thus it spans. Claims 1–3 exclude d<=2 and K=2.

claims.claim: In a minimum-order counterexample, every outneighborhood S has minimum internal outdegree at most ceil(d/K)-1.
claims.evidence: Here |S|=d<n. If its minimum internal outdegree r>=1, minimality applies the target to D[S], giving a cycle of length at most ceil(d/r). Since the ambient girth exceeds K, ceil(d/r)>K, equivalently r<d/K. For integral r this is r<=ceil(d/K)-1; r=0 also satisfies it.

claims.claim: Every minimum-order counterexample satisfies n>=3d+2-ceil(d/K). In particular, when K=3 it satisfies 3d+2-ceil(d/3)<=n<=3d.
claims.evidence: Choose v with indegree at least d and u in S=N+(v) with at least d-ceil(d/K)+1 outneighbors outside S. Such outneighbors are neither v nor in N-(v), since those choices create a 2- or 3-cycle. The disjoint sets {v}, S, N-(v), and these outneighbors therefore total at least 3d+2-ceil(d/K). If K=3, ceil(n/d)=3 also gives n<=3d.

claims.claim: If n<=2d+ceil((d+1)/2), then D has a directed cycle of length at most 3.
claims.evidence: Assume no cycle through length 3 and trim to d-outregular. For v of indegree at least d, the oriented graph on S=N+(v) has a vertex u with at most floor((d-1)/2) internal outneighbors. Thus u has at least ceil((d+1)/2) outneighbors outside S, none in {v} or N-(v). Counting the resulting disjoint sets gives n>=1+2d+ceil((d+1)/2), contradicting the hypothesis.
claims.search_method: Exact extremal arc count and disjoint-set proof audit

claims.claim: For d=3 and n<=9, D has a directed cycle of length at most 3.
claims.evidence: Without a cycle through length 3, each three-vertex outneighborhood has an internal sink u. Its three outneighbors avoid {v}, N+(v), and N-(v), giving n>=7+d-(v). For n<=9 every vertex would have indegree at most two, contradicting average indegree three. Independently, the checker exhaustively returned UNSAT for n=7,8,9; n<=6 follows from the exact antiparallel arc count.
claims.search_method: Direct proof plus exhaustive exact row-mask search with symmetry normalization

claims.claim: For d=3 and n=10, D has a directed cycle of length at most 4.
claims.evidence: The hand argument is sound: absence of cycles through length 4 forces 3-in/3-out regularity; partitioning around v into its three outneighbors S, three inneighbors I, and three nonneighbors R yields the stated contradiction from arcs S→R. Independently, the checker proved (10,3,K=4) UNSAT after 191,232 nodes.
claims.search_method: Direct partition/counting proof plus exhaustive exact row-mask search

claims.claim: The target holds for semicomplete digraphs.
claims.evidence: An antiparallel pair gives a valid 2-cycle. Otherwise the digraph is a tournament. Minimum outdegree at least one rules out a transitive tournament, and a shortest tournament cycle must be a triangle by its first-to-third chord. Also d<=(n-1)/2, so ceil(n/d)>=3.

claims.claim: The target holds for every n<=10.
claims.evidence: The case split is complete: d=1,2 use claims 1–2; 2d>=n uses claim 3; d=3 uses claims 11–12; the only remaining pairs are (9,4) and (10,4), both covered by claim 10. The independent checker also returned UNSAT for every nontrivial pair through n=10, including 280,498 nodes for (10,2,5), 191,232 for (10,3,4), and 23,244 for (10,4,3).
claims.search_method: Complete parameter split plus exhaustive exact row-mask search

claims.claim: For every 1<=d<n, the circulant digraph on Z_n with arcs i→i+s mod n for 1<=s<=d has directed girth exactly ceil(n/d).
claims.evidence: If a directed cycle has l increments in {1,...,d}, their positive sum is a positive multiple of n, so ld>=n and l>=ceil(n/d). For L=ceil(n/d), the increments d,...,d,n-(L-1)d are all in {1,...,d}, sum to n, and have distinct proper partial sums strictly between 0 and n. They therefore form a simple directed L-cycle.
claims.witness: For L=ceil(n/d), use the cycle 0→d→2d→...→(L-1)d→0, whose final increment modulo n is n-(L-1)d.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for a proof of the conjecture for all finite digraphs or an explicit counterexample with girth strictly exceeding ceil(n/d). The draft expressly supplies neither: its circulant family attains equality and hence is not a counterexample, while the other results cover only special regimes, reductions, and approximations. Those results are nevertheless correct and material, so this is valid partial progress. The draft's claimed resolution PARTIAL and its final disclaimer accurately describe that coverage and do not overclaim a full solution.
